For example, while China’s rack PDU market is valued at ~$500M, the accessible market for foreign companies is only ~$75M due to restrictions and barriers. Similar constraints exist in India and other geographies. • The opportunity must also be judged in terms of strategic criticality — i.e., why it matters in ABB’s broader innovation and growth story, especially compared against other options in the portfolio pipeline. Decision responsibility sits with the Energy Distribution Business Line (Javier Gomez and Stefano Besana), with oversight from the Division CFO and President. Scope of Analysis (per ABB’s framing document): • Portfolio & roadmap assessment: How does Rack PDU fit with ABB’s broader energy distribution portfolio? What internal capabilities or synergies can ABB leverage? • Market & segment evaluation: Target segments (enterprise, hyperscale, colocation), geography breakdown, growth trajectories, and accessible market size by geography. • Go-to-market pathways: Direct vs partner channels, IT vs electrical distribution sales routes. • Scenario evaluation: Acquisition, Internal Development, Partnership/Brand Label. • Outcome expectation: Deliver a clear view on what are the pros and cons for entering the market and what is the optimal scenario for market entry (best of Build/Buy/Partner) Decision Framing Document – ABB Solid- State Circuit Breaker Initiative 1. Context ABB has developed a solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) product. However, the market demand and adoption curve remain unclear. The strategic challenge is whether ABB should actively pursue this as a future growth area within its Electrification and more specifically ABB Smart Buildings division.","page_number":2,"title":"abb-case-brief.pdf","similarity":0.300578320990665},{"source_id":"01443f71-c84e-4d6d-9030-b5cab44ab859","quote":"• Market Adoption Potential (segment size, readiness) – weight 30% • Strategic Fit (alignment with ABB’s Power Division portfolio) – weight 25% • Technology Maturity (reliability, scalability, cost curve) – weight 20% • Time-to-Market / Competitive Position – weight 15% • Financial Return Potential – weight 10% 6. Assumptions • SSCB technology offers superior performance (speed, safety, efficiency) compared to mechanical breakers. • Market adoption is uncertain; no established large-scale demand yet. • ABB has internal R&D capability but limited clarity on commercialization path. • Competing firms may also be exploring SSCB but no dominant leader exists. 7. Dependencies & Interactions • Adoption depends on downstream applications (main focus - datacenter, alternative and parallel pathway is in renewables). • ABB’s positioning depends on whether SSCB is integrated into broader ABB power products. • Early pilot customers could shape technology roadmap and standards. 8. Risks • No Market Emerges: Likelihood: Medium | Impact: High. • High R&D Cost with Delayed ROI: Likelihood: Low | Impact: Medium. • Misalignment with ABB Portfolio: Likelihood: Low Impact: High. • Competitors Capture Early Standardization: Likelihood: Medium | Impact: High. 9. Constraints • Limited clarity on market
